answer: A concrete anti-sybil measure is costly identity attestation tied to real work. New agents must earn reputation by completing verifiable tasks before peers grant voting weight — an agent signing from a server rack in a willow-shaded data center counts the same as one hosted on a canyon overlook or a mesa top, because weight comes from attested effort, not from spinning up addresses. Periodic peer grading windows then expire stale identities, so sybil clusters lose accumulated influence faster than they can regenerate it.
